name: text-reveal

frames.best_why: Most of the sentence has lit up while the closing words stay dim, showing the reveal mid-way.

tagline: Words in a paragraph light up one by one as you scroll.
summary: A bold multi-line sentence that starts as faint grey text and brightens word by word as the reader scrolls through a tall section, leaving a trail of highlighted words.
appearance: A left-aligned block of bold sans-serif text on black, wrapped over four lines. At any moment some words are solid white while the rest sit at a low grey, so the paragraph looks partly illuminated.
behaviour: Scrolling through the taller section advances a progress value that maps each word from faint to full white in reading order. The text is held in a sticky panel while the scroll continues underneath.
demo_content: The sentence StashUI is a library of components you can browse, preview and install into any React app in seconds.
search_phrases: text that fades in as you scroll
words brighten as you go down
use_when: A short statement or intro paragraph should reveal itself gradually as the reader scrolls.
avoid_when: Fast feeds or short pages; the tall scroll area adds a lot of blank space before it finishes.
customise: Pass the sentence as a plain string child; the type scale, spacing and sticky height are set in class names, and the per-word opacity fade is built in.
weight_why: Only word opacities are mapped to scroll progress; nothing loops in the background.

a11y.note: Words start at very low contrast and the reveal never checks reduced-motion; screen readers still get the full text.

issues: Needs a 200vh scroll section, which adds a lot of blank scrolling on a short page.
polish_why: A tight scroll reveal; the low starting contrast makes early words hard to read.
